title: Programming an Unreal video game with AI
author: MMPhotoshop
selftext:
I love programming, but I hate character rigging and animation.

I’ve never really managed to make a game featuring a human character because the animation is just too complex...

I used Claude, and in five hours, I burned through a whole week's worth of usage. It still couldn't pull it off. I created at least 50 different poses, and it’s still incredibly complex.

In my game the character floats without gravity and it's absurd.

Codex 6 Astra and Sol 6.1 is collaborating with ChatGPT, and has also worked with Claude Code, to find a solution. You have no idea of the mathematical formulas required, the constraints, the muscles, the bones, it's madness.  

ChatGPT has found a way to keep Codex from hitting its limits (at least not right away). There are analyses hundreds of pages long that I’m not reading. Codebases thousands of lines long.

I don’t know how game developers do it.

It took eight hours just to get the character to sit on the toilet.

Since it’s a space game... it took us about 30 minutes to an hour to build the spaceship and create a physically accurate, complete space environment. We’ve been working on the character's poses and movements for three days now; Claude Code actually ran out of credits on the very first day after five hours. Every day I work there from 8 to 10 or 12 hours. I’d put in even more time if the tools didn't keep freezing up.

I even had to create a bone editing system that was better than Unreal and Blender in the game, and that really got us ahead.

I’m not sure how other game developers usually handle this. I’ll probably release this game in two years. I won't tell you what it's about. But it will be two years with AI, hoping they don't increase prices. I’d really love to use local AI, but how do you get the same speed and power as GPT-6 Astra right at home?

comments.author: Limp_Bus3865
comments.body: First of all, you won't need two years because ai is getting better and it will probably solve animations in a few months. Second of all, do some research. There are AIs now that do 90% of rigging, especially if it is a human. Then after that you can use a mocap tool to record yourself on camera and copy that animation. In case of other stuff, you can always have a genAI gemerate you a video of animation and then use another ai to copy that animation from video iterativelly until it looks right. Some things like skinning can be adjusted in blender manually, no need to waste tokens

replies.author: MMPhotoshop

replies.author: redditscraperbot2
replies.body:
Jokes aside, it reads to me like you are trying to reinvent the wheel here. This is unreal correct? You do have markerless mocap available at a relatively high quality and AI video as input does work. But I see you don't actually want use mocap (even though it's the most pain free solution with the tools available). You could also take a look at tools like kimodo that turns text into character motions. Current models are more than capable of taking those motions, like sitting, laying them so your toilet dude can be sitting on the toilet while his upper body is reading a newspaper. 

Another option is cascadeur with live link. Totally works, but it is a paid program, but all the AI needs to do is make keyframes and it can use clever interpolation to turn it into a full animations and import ti back into ue5 relatively pain free.

comments.author: jobehi
comments.body: but why reinventing the wheel and even use AI for this ? there are a lot of open source projects to design characters easily, to rig them and to use already captured motions. all free, open sources and CC.

replies.author: MMPhotoshop
replies.body: I don't know them, can you tell me the best you would use for a character who moves freely in space? Thank you very much.

replies.author: jobehi
replies.body:
[https://static.makehumancommunity.org/makehuman.html](https://static.makehumancommunity.org/makehuman.html) : to create your character, fully rigged  
[https://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/](https://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/) : all  possible human motions you can ever imagine : compatible with your character.  
[https://www.mixamo.com/#/](https://www.mixamo.com/#/) : in case of you didn't find what you're looking for in the cmu dataset

comments.author: YesImYou
comments.body: It takes one, maybe two days, to learn how to do basic animations in blender. Not every single thing has to be made by AI bruh

comments.author: trai1er_dude
comments.body: I think your prompts just aren't very good, you need to improve your prompts, if you type in bold sometimes it helps and make sure you include full stops and commas. I prompted "make the game really good" and got a game almost as good as gta6 in ue5. What can also help is make a better game engine yourself, i just prompted "make ue8 but better" and i've got an incredible game engine in 5 minutes which is better than ue8.
